name: BCA Assay
description: Bicinchoninic acid (BCA) colorimetric assay for total protein quantification. Compatible with most detergents used in cell lysis. Results in ~30–60 min.
source_note: General educational template for BCA protein assay (e.g., Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit).

steps.title: Prepare BSA standard curve
steps.description: Prepare a series of BSA protein standards by serial dilution in the same buffer used for your samples (e.g., RIPA). Typical range: 0, 25, 125, 250, 500, 750, 1000, 1500, 2000 µg/mL.

reagents.name: BSA (bovine serum albumin) stock solution (2 mg/mL)
Sample diluent (same as your lysis buffer)

steps.notes: Use the diluent (blank without protein) as the 0 µg/mL standard. Prepare standards in the same buffer as samples to minimize matrix effects.

steps.title: Dilute protein samples
steps.description: Dilute unknown protein samples in sample diluent if necessary to bring expected concentration within the standard curve range (0–2000 µg/mL). Run samples in duplicate.
steps.notes: If unsure of concentration, test a 1:5 and 1:10 dilution. Both should fall within standard curve range for reliable quantification.

steps.title: Add samples and standards to microplate
steps.description: Pipette 25 µL of each standard and sample (duplicate or triplicate) into appropriate wells of a 96-well flat-bottom plate.
steps.notes: Record plate map. Include blank (0 µg/mL BSA) to correct for background.

steps.title: Prepare and add BCA working reagent
steps.description: Prepare BCA Working Reagent by mixing Reagent A and Reagent B at 50:1 ratio. Add 200 µL of working reagent to each well. Tap plate gently to mix.
steps.notes: Final volume per well: 25 µL sample + 200 µL working reagent = 225 µL total.
steps.warnings: BCA working reagent contains NaOH — corrosive. Avoid skin contact.

steps.title: Incubate at 37°C
steps.description: Cover the plate and incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes. The solution will develop a purple color proportional to protein concentration.
steps.notes: For lower detection limit, incubate at 60°C for 30 min (enhanced BCA protocol). Color develops proportionally to protein concentration.

steps.title: Cool and read absorbance
steps.description: Allow plate to cool to room temperature for 5 min. Read absorbance at 562 nm using a microplate reader.
steps.notes: Read within 10 min of removing from incubator for consistent results.

steps.title: Calculate protein concentration
steps.description: Generate a standard curve (Abs 562 vs. BSA concentration). Use linear regression to calculate the protein concentration of each unknown sample (accounting for any dilutions made).
steps.notes: R² of standard curve should be >0.99. Discard outlier duplicates. Multiply by dilution factor to get original concentration.
